evidence.text: Reason for referral: Recurrent episodes of palpitations and lightheadedness over the past three months in a 75-year-old man with hypertension.

Findings: Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a single premature atrial complex. Normal axis. PR interval 172 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 430 ms.
Impression: Sinus rhythm with one premature atrial complex, otherwise normal tracing.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at 60%. No regional wall motion abnormalities. Mild left atrial enlargement. Trace mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Normal left ventricular systolic function with mild left atrial enlargement.

LIPID PANEL
Total Cholesterol: 198 mg/dL
LDL Cholesterol: 118 mg/dL (H)
HDL Cholesterol: 46 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 170 mg/dL (H)

BASIC METABOLIC PANEL
Sodium: 141 mmol/L
Potassium: 4.0 mmol/L
Chloride: 104 mmol/L
CO2: 26 mmol/L
BUN: 18 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Glucose: 104 mg/dL (H)
Calcium: 9.2 mg/dL

Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily
Amlodipine 5 mg by mouth once daily
Rosuvastatin 10 mg by mouth once daily

EXAM:
General: alert, no acute distress.
Neck: no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs or gallops.
Lungs: clear bilaterally.
Extremities: warm, no edema.
